properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Idea 13 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 (Anthony's VS Code `--call` guide, 2b95bb4, 2026-10-02), in its words: "A hub address book: hub pins that carry a store location, and a tool that resolves 'where is member X's store on this machine'. Fixes 13."

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so this is not re-opened:
- Which designs a hub tracks is its declared dependencies. That is upstream.rs's "the child list is the manifest", and it is accepted in req:one-search-reaches-every-design-a-hub-tracks, which reaches each one "a committed export read from disk, or a design at an address".
- How a design is watched: by asking its server, never a file (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy).
Measured 2026-10-02 (fact:root-cause-a-local-hubs-list-is-its-watch-manifest-but-the-hub-skill-names-the-mcp-config-and-no-pin-says-where-a-store-is-2026-10-02): the list is readable under `--call`. What no record holds is how THIS machine reaches each member. The only open part is how, for a door agent with no MCP server running.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORT'S: a declared dependency carries a store path. ⚠️ As a committed field this runs against the accepted rule above, a design is never watched by a file, and against the committed manifest being machine-independent. So it is listed for completeness, not offered as live.
(b) A PER-MACHINE ADDRESS BOOK, never committed: graph_id → where its store is on this machine, kept beside the user's reflow2 config. A read-only tool resolves it ("where is design X here?"), and the committed manifest keeps only ids and addresses. Cheap, and it answers the reporter's "project file of store paths, for now".
(c) EVERY LOCAL DESIGN AT A STABLE LOCAL ADDRESS: one local registry (`--registry-root … --http` on a fixed port) serves the machine's designs at /g/<id>/, so the existing design_address watch and the accepted hub search work unchanged. This fits the blueprint best. It needs a long-running process, and the door cannot reach a server today: `--remote URL --call X` silently drops the call (measured 2026-10-02).
(d) EXTEND THE POINTER: `.reflow2.toml` [[also]] entries already name other designs by id, address and role, and are listed but never opened.
(e) NOTHING NEW: the hub skill says that under the door the member list is the declared dependencies, and the person keeps the store paths.

COST AND COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- Opening a member's local store from the hub collides with the single writer. If its own session holds it, the door reads a snapshot, and a snapshot has no text index: search_design and topic_report answer "NOTHING MATCHED" (fact:root-cause-a-held-design-answers-search-through-the-door-with-a-false-nothing-matched-2026-10-02). So (b) is only as good as that defect's fix.
- (c) moves a Copilot-only user toward running a server, which is what the door exists to avoid. It also depends on dec:idea-a-one-shot-call-reaches-the-design-where-it-is-served.
- A per-machine record is something else to go stale. A moved store would make (b) point at a frozen copy, the class of fact:an-agent-opened-in-a-moved-designs-folder-is-served-the-frozen-store-2026-09-27.

DATED NOTE 2026-10-05 (triage of art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05): RAISED AGAIN in Anthony's VS Code work log (entries of 2026-10-01 and 10-02, on 0.76.0), with new detail:
- The work hub keeps its member list in two files: a committed one naming each member design, and a generated per-machine one holding absolute store paths. That is option (b), kept by hand.
- The 2026-10-02 ruling left this open partly because the reporter's work use was one design. The log shows that is no longer so: at least three member designs were pinned or captured from the work hub on 2026-10-01 and 10-02, through external_dependency, upstream_status and compare_designs.
- The same log asks for a one-call member tool and for hub skill text on where a member's store lives: dec:idea-one-call-adds-a-member-design-to-a-local-hub and dec:idea-the-hub-skill-teaches-how-a-member-design-is-kept-under-the-door.
properties.name: OPEN — on one machine with no running server, how does a hub driven through the `--call` door reach each design it tracks: a per-machine record of where each one's store is, a local server address for each, or nothing new?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an open question from a field report's idea list, under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. Only the HOW is open; which designs a hub tracks, and that a design is watched by address, are already accepted. Nothing here is promoted; that is Anthony's word.
